key_insight: Instead of enumerating all subsets of specifications, the paper computes in one fixed-point the relation between product-game states and the sets of properties realizable from them, then synthesizes strategies that achieve maximal realizable property sets using symbolic Boolean goal variables and monotonicity.
problem_solved: Handles LTLf synthesis when multiple (possibly conflicting) properties exist and satisfying all may be impossible, avoiding exponential blow-up from subset enumeration while producing maximal best‑effort strategies.
method: Construct a product game for the system and encode each property as a Boolean goal variable to represent goal combinations compactly.
Perform a single fixed-point computation that relates game states to realizable goal sets, leveraging monotonicity to propagate and prune possibilities.
Implement a fully symbolic algorithm that represents exponentially many goal combinations succinctly and extracts strategies that maximize realizable property sets.
impact: Makes multi-property synthesis scalable and practical for industry-scale reactive systems by avoiding combinatorial subset enumeration and producing best‑effort controllers when full specification satisfaction is impossible.
visual_elements: Diagram of product-game nodes with Boolean goal variables attached, showing mapping from states to realizable goal sets.

paper_authors: Christoph Weinhuber, Yannik Schnitzer, Alessandro Abate, David Parker, Giuseppe De Giacomo
